features.profile_configuration: bounded active-profile language configuration foundation implemented
features.rtl_ltr_context: HTML attributes and stable body classes implemented
features.directory_routing: directory-style storefront routing and safe current-path language URLs implemented
features.wordpress_locale_switching: public locale filters and switch_to_locale bridge implemented for storefront requests
features.language_switcher: accessible style-neutral shortcode/public filter surface implemented
features.multilingual_seo: localized canonical targets plus hreflang alternates and x-default implemented for indexable frontend routes
features.translation_repository: versioned entry/revision tables with published lookup and source hashes implemented
features.translation_workflow: append-only draft/review/published workflow with pre-publish validation and published-revision isolation implemented
features.translation_import_export: versioned JSON, CSV and XLIFF 1.2 interchange foundation with preflight analysis and draft-only import application
features.translation_import_safety: size/record limits, duplicate identity rejection, schema validation, DTD/entity rejection for XLIFF and no automatic publication
features.woocommerce_entity_mapping: product text, product category/tag/attribute term text and attribute labels mapped to translation keys without commercial-data duplication
features.translated_permalinks: language-specific product, product category/tag and global attribute term slugs routed through indexed current routes plus historical aliases
features.translated_permalink_redirects: previous translated slugs retained as same-language aliases that resolve to the current translated entity permalink
features.woocommerce_language_context: localized storefront language persisted in WooCommerce session and captured through WC_Order CRUD meta for classic and Store API checkout
features.async_translation_context: AJAX/REST entity translation allowed only when a valid WooCommerce session language is restored
features.order_language_snapshot: language code, WordPress locale and text direction frozen on the order for later rendering
features.order_language_rendering_scope: isolated locale/translation scope implemented for WooCommerce transactional order notifications, manual resend and programmatic document rendering
features.historical_language_rendering: stored order locale and translation code can render historical orders even after a language is disabled

notes: WordPress minimum/tested ranges will be finalized with the Phase 0 environment audit and compatibility matrix.
WordPress Core's singular canonical is localized through get_canonical_url; non-singular indexable frontend views receive a filterable Multilingual canonical in wp_head.
Every enabled language receives a same-entity hreflang alternate and x-default points to the configured default language rather than the fallback language.
Canonical and hreflang targets are generated without current tracking, filter, nonce or action query parameters.

Translated permalink keys are woocommerce.product.{ID}.slug and woocommerce.term.{taxonomy}.{TERM_ID}.slug; product/category/tag/global-attribute identities remain the original WordPress/WooCommerce IDs.
Translation DB schema v2 adds indexed current-route and historical-alias tables; it does not duplicate products, terms, stock, SKU, prices or order state.
Outgoing links use the target language route when published; incoming translated slugs are resolved back to the existing technical source slug before WordPress/WooCommerce executes the query.
Changing a translated slug keeps the previous translated slug as a redirect alias to the current same-language permalink.
A language with no published slug translation falls back to the technical source slug, never to another language's slug.
Source-slug and translated-route collisions are rejected before a reviewed slug translation can publish.
Translation interchange exports current or published revision snapshots only and deliberately excludes author/reviewer user IDs, secrets and customer transaction data.
Import preflight classifies new, conflicting, unchanged and invalid records before writing. Application aborts on invalid records and changed records enter the normal workflow as new drafts only.
XLIFF parsing rejects DTD/entity declarations and uses network-disabled XML parsing; XML support depends on PHP DOM being available.
Search, 404, feed, trackback, preview, admin, AJAX and REST requests remain outside normal storefront permalink rewriting unless an existing explicit async language contract allows link localization.
WooCommerce product IDs, variation IDs, taxonomy/term IDs, SKU, prices, stock, tax, cart and order state remain WooCommerce-owned.
Customer-specific language lists live in the versioned customer profile rather than generic package code.
